questions.question: Describe the founding and early history of Genadendal.
questions.expected_answer: Founded in 1738 by Georg Schmidt of the Moravian Church in the Baviaanskloof among Hessequa Khoikhoi; he taught reading and writing (first school for Khoikhoi) and farming; in 1742 he baptised five Khoikhoi including Vehettge Magdalena Tikkuie, angering the Dutch Reformed Church, and was forced to leave in 1744; Magdalena kept the congregation together; Moravians returned in 1792 and restarted the mission, renamed Genadendal (Valley of Grace) in 1806.

questions.question: Explain the significance of Genadendal.
questions.expected_answer: Refuge from forced farm labour where Khoikhoi (and freed slaves after 1838) could live with families on land not owned by farmers; education - schools and the first teachers' training college (1838), printing press; skills - carpentry, blacksmithing, cutlery; community and identity; inspired other missions (Elim, Mamre). Limits: strict rules, loss of some customs, residents did not own the land. Today a heritage site; Mandela named his residence Genadendal (1995).

questions.question: Explain the work of Bleek and Lloyd and why it is important.
questions.expected_answer: Wilhelm Bleek (German linguist) and Lucy Lloyd recorded the !Xam language and culture from !Xam informants, such as //Kabbo and Dia!kwain, who were prisoners at the Breakwater and lived in Bleek's Mowbray home from 1870; over 12 000 pages of stories, beliefs, history and drawings. Importance: !Xam language died out, so knowledge was preserved; helps interpret rock art; gives a voice to the San; UNESCO Memory of the World (1997); coat of arms motto in !Xam. Critically, it was made in unequal colonial circumstances.
